articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed, avg 11 published/cycle (50 yesterday)

topSourceShare.source: Reuters / Al Jazeera Online / Bloomberg Business (tie)

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, there is no pause gate, and every target is met except science, at 4 against 5, which the 2026-09-26 decision allows on a thin-science day. Latin American datelines recovered from 0% to 5% without a change, which supports yesterday's reading that the gap was supply, not selection.
weakestArea: Science is 4 against 5 for the second day running, and it comes from only two outlets (Phys.org ×3, STAT). The fix by policy is wider science sources, not a higher floor. US datelines sit exactly on the 25% ceiling, and five of the fourteen are the bare country name "United States" rather than a city.
watching: Hormuz and the Gulf: Iran now says the tankers were hit by mines, and coastguards are forming a joint Red Sea arrangement.
Gaza: Oxfam reports poisoned water and the Yellow Line keeps displacing people, while settlers entered a Jericho neighbourhood in the West Bank.
Nigeria: gunmen hit a Delta State campaign event and the naira slid on election risk, and Abuja has protested to South Africa over killings of Nigerians.
Ukraine at sea: Ukraine says it sank a Russian corvette off Libya, and NATO warned about a Russian nuclear-armed satellite.
Deutsche Bank: two stories on financing of meatpackers and tank parts, likely to draw follow-ups.
COP31 ended without a deal, so watch for national responses and a fallback text.
coverageGaps: Science came from two outlets only (Phys.org, STAT); health, climate and physics journals were absent.
Tech is 18 of 56 (32%) and leans on Chinese tech press and security news, while science is thin.
Six datelines are bare country names ("United States" ×5, "South Africa") rather than cities.
context: This is the third straight day with all five cycles completed. Cycles averaged 1123s against 910s yesterday, with the selector at 169s, the writer at 143s and the editor at 93s. Source spread is the widest this week: 58 outlets, none above 11%.
